description: CSUTLDTC, the called date-validation subprogram, invoked as the @Service it became. LS-DATE='2022-07-19' and LS-DATE-FORMAT='<AD-MM-DD ' are this case's two LINKAGE SECTION parameters (L84-L85); LS-RESULT PIC X(80) (L86) is the output and is asserted below as the single WS_MESSAGE_80 line. This program opens no file and is reached by no JCL, so it seeds no dataset, writes no record and takes no job parameter - its entire observable behaviour is the 80 bytes L97 moves into LS-RESULT and the severity L98 moves into RETURN-CODE, which is 3 here and is deliberately not normalised to 4, 8 or 12. Expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED from the 01 WS-MESSAGE declaration at L42-L57, the arm literal at L142 and the group move at L122, never captured from a COBOL run, which is impossible here: no Language Environment CEE* service exists in this environment, so CEEDAYS cannot be called at all. The thirteen declared spans sum mechanically to 80 and the line is encoded US-ASCII rather than in any platform default. Arm 7 of the ten-arm EVALUATE at L128-L149: FC-BAD-PIC-STRING, 88-level VALUE X'000309D659C3C5C5' (L68), whose two leading halfwords DECODE to severity 0x0003 = 3 and message number 0x09D6 = 2518. The arm moves the literal 'Bad Pic String ' into WS-RESULT at L142, and it is reproduced here exactly as the source spells it - fifteen characters including the trailing space the author baked inside the quotes, so WS-RESULT PIC X(15) receives no pad byte of its own. Both numbers are read out of that hex rather than interpolated from the neighbouring arms, which matters because the nine tokens are not consecutive - 0x09D7, which would be 2519, is absent from the set entirely - and the trailing 59C3C5C5 is the severity-control byte and the facility identifier 'CEE', which take no part in the message. This is the THIRD and structurally distinct route to arm 7. In case15 the mask contains a letter that begins no recognised token and in case16 the YEAR role is declared twice; here the fault is neither, because the era field is OPENED at the very first picture character and never closed. The rejection is therefore taken at that first character, before any letter of the mask is examined at all, which is what separates this case from case15's unrecognised-letter route. It is equally not the 2509 Invalid Era of case09: 'AD' is a supported era name, but an era field that is never closed yields no name to compare against the AD/BC repertoire, so the failure is purely structural rather than a matter of the era's content. The precedence this pins is the whole point of the case - the missing delimiter is caught while the picture string is still being scanned, and so precedes the completeness check applied once scanning ends. That check would have had something to say: this mask declares no year field anywhere, so had the era been closed as '<AD>-MM-DD' the outcome would have been 2507 for insufficient data instead of 2518. The date itself is the well-formed one from case01 and is never examined, because the picture string is rejected before the input is scanned - yet WS-DATE still reports it, and reports it corrupted. L122 overwrites the clean copy made at L107-L108 with a GROUP move whose leftmost two bytes are the Vstring-length halfword 0x000A, set at L105 from LENGTH OF LS-DATE - the DECLARED PIC X(10) width, never a trimmed length - so only the first eight characters, '2022-07-', survive into PIC X(10) and the trailing '19' is discarded. Those two leading bytes are non-printable and are written explicitly as \u0000 and \u000A rather than left for a reader to infer from an invisible span. WS-DATE-FMT is set at L111-L113 and is not a target of L122, so the mask is echoed clean, and that matters most here because the mask is the faulty parameter: the case shows the offending picture string reproduced verbatim in the message that rejects it. The three FILLER literals survive INITIALIZE WS-MESSAGE at L90, which leaves FILLER untouched, so 'Mesg Code:', 'TstDate:' and 'Mask used:' appear in this output as they do in every other.
